01 · The list

Greetings and phrases,
level by level

Greetings and set phrases in Korean: hello and goodbye, thank you and sorry, please, yes and no, and the social phrases that make a first conversation work, from the TOPIK vocabulary lists with readings and meanings.

In Lock&Learn Korean these words sit in their level packs (Beginner 1, Beginner 2), one per glance on the widget: a word waits in hangul with its romanization; one tap reveals the meaning and a real sentence. Beginner 1 is free; every other pack opens with a free preview and another word unlocks daily.

Type to filter by hangul, romanization or meaning. Flashcards hides the meaning until you tap a row; Shuffle deals the list in a new order.

03 · Questions

Asked and
answered

What are the basic greetings in Korean?

The 30 greetings and phrases below come from the TOPIK vocabulary lists with their readings and meanings. The beginner-level ones come with a real sentence.

Which TOPIK levels are these words from?

30 from TOPIK I. The level chip on each row says where the word sits, so you can stop at your level or read ahead. Beginner-level words carry a real example sentence; the rest show word, romanization and meaning, with their sentences in the app.

How do I learn greetings and phrases words on my iPhone Lock Screen?

Install Lock&Learn Korean, then touch and hold your Lock Screen, tap Customize, tap the widget area and choose Lock&Learn Korean. Enable the level packs these words come from (Beginner 1, Beginner 2). A word waits in hangul with its romanization; one tap reveals the meaning and a real sentence.

Is Lock&Learn Korean free?

Yes. The app is free on iOS: Beginner 1 is free, every other pack opens with a free preview, and another word unlocks daily. Lock&Learn+ is an optional upgrade that opens every pack at once, offered as a yearly plan or a one-time lifetime purchase.
